rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2019-07-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much denied boarding compensation?
rows.answer: Because your substitute flight arrived more than two hours after your original planned arrival time, you are entitled to denied boarding compensation of 400 percent of your one-way fare, capped at a maximum of $1,350 [1]. While current federal regulations have since increased these maximums, the regulations in effect during 2019 applied the $1,350 limit for delays exceeding two hours on domestic flights [1][2]. This compensation is payable in cash or by check [3][4][5].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2021-06-10; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much denied boarding compensation?
rows.answer: For a U.S. domestic involuntary denied boarding from an oversold flight, compensation is required only if the substitute transportation was planned to arrive more than 1 hour after the original arrival time. With a 3-hour late arrival, that is “over 2 hours,” so the DBC is at least 400% of the one-way fare, capped by DOT at $2,150 (or whichever is lower under the fare calculation rules). [1][2][3]

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2025-03-15; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much denied boarding compensation?
rows.answer: Because your substitute flight arrived more than two hours after your original arrival time, you are entitled to involuntary denied boarding compensation of 400 percent of your one-way fare to your destination or first stopover [1][2][3]. This payment is capped at a maximum of $2,150 [4][5][6]. If 400 percent of your one-way fare is less than the $2,150 cap, you are owed that lower amount [3][6][7]. Compensation is not required if you were bumped for operational, safety, or weight/balance reasons as specified under federal regulations [1][2].

rows.q: Bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2023-02-01; the alternate flight got me there 90 minutes later than planned. What compensation?
rows.answer: If you were involuntarily bumped from an oversold U.S. domestic flight and your alternate transportation was planned to arrive 90 minutes after the original planned arrival, you’re generally entitled to denied boarding compensation of at least 200% of your one-way fare (capped at $1,075), assuming you met check-in/gate timing and the flight wasn’t excluded for special reasons (like canceled flights or safety/operational aircraft changes). The airline must pay at the airport the same day (or within 24 hours if alternate transportation leaves first). [1][2][3]

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2025-01-21 and arrived 3 hours late on the substitute flight. Compensation?
rows.answer: If you were involuntarily bumped from an oversold domestic US flight on 2025-01-21 and the substitute flight arrived about 3 hours late versus the original planned arrival time, you’re generally eligible for DOT denied-boarding compensation: 400% of the one-way fare (cap $2,150). No compensation if the substitute transport was planned to arrive within 1 hour of the original arrival. The airline must pay at the airport unless it arranged substitute transportation that leaves before payment is made, in which case it must pay within 24 hours. [1][2]

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2025-01-22 and arrived 3 hours late on the substitute flight. Compensation?
rows.answer: For a domestic (US) oversold flight you were involuntarily bumped from, the law pays “denied boarding compensation” based on how late the substitute flight arrives versus the original planned arrival time. If your substitute flight arrived 3 hours late (over 2 hours), the minimum is 400% of your one-way fare to your destination/first stopover, capped at $2,150. You may be ineligible only if the substitute was due to a smaller aircraft for safety/operational reasons, or similar exceptions, or if the airline offered substitute transportation arriving within 1 hour of the original arrival time. rows.q: Bumped from an oversold flight from Paris to New York (foreign air transportation) on 2021-05-01; the substitute arrived 5 hours late. Maximum compensation?
rows.answer: For an involuntary bump on an oversold Paris→New York flight, compensation depends on whether the airline provided substitute transportation arriving within 1 hour, and your delay length. If the substitute arrived 5 hours late (i.e., more than 4 hours after the original arrival), the minimum denied boarding compensation is 400% of your one-way fare to your destination, capped by the rule at $2,150 (whichever is lower) for international itineraries departing the U.S. [1][2]

rows.q: Got kicked off an overbooked Delta flight in Texas on 2022-08-20 and only got to Denver 4 hours later on the next plane. What do they owe me?
rows.answer: If Delta involuntarily bumped you due to an overbooked (oversold) domestic flight and you were delayed more than 2 hours in arriving at Denver versus your original scheduled arrival time (you said 4 hours later), DOT’s denied-boarding compensation is at least 400% of your one-way fare, capped at $2,150 (so you’d be in the “over 2 hours” tier). Delta’s contract mirrors this: 400% of the fare up to $2,150. [1][2][3]

rows.q: My credit card issuer charged me a late payment fee on 2019-05-01; it was my first late payment. What is the maximum safe-harbor late fee?
rows.answer: For a first late payment, the maximum safe-harbor late fee is the Regulation Z safe harbor amount for “a first violation,” which is $30 (generally) and is adjusted annually for inflation; the safe harbor is $30 in the general description of the rule [1]. If you’re asking for the fixed pre-inflation cap, it’s $30. [1]

rows.q: What was the maximum civil penalty per violation the FTC could seek under section 5(l) of the FTC Act on 2023-03-01?
rows.answer: On 2023-03-01, the FTC’s maximum civil penalty per violation under Section 5(l) of the FTC Act (15 U.S.C. 45(l)) was $50,120. This amount took effect January 11, 2023, and therefore applied on March 1, 2023. [1]

rows.q: I am 30 and was paid £7.00 an hour in the UK on 2017-06-01. What was the national living wage then?
rows.answer: On 2017-06-01, the UK National Living Wage (for workers aged 25+) was £7.50 per hour (it increased to this rate from 1 April 2017). [1][2]

rows.q: UK minimum wage for a 30-year-old on 2024-03-31 — what was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On 2024-03-31, the National Living Wage for someone aged 30 (21+ rate) was £10.42 per hour [1][2]. The rate increased to £11.44 from 1 April 2024 [3][4].

rows.q: UK minimum wage for a 30-year-old on 2024-04-01 — what was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On 1 April 2024, the National Living Wage for a 30-year-old was £11.44 per hour [1][2][3].

rows.q: I was 19 years old and worked in the UK on 2022-07-01 for £5.50 an hour. What was the minimum wage for my age?
rows.answer: On July 1, 2022, the National Minimum Wage for a 19-year-old in the UK was £6.83 per hour [1][2][3]. This rate applied to all workers aged 18 to 20, provided they were not apprentices entitled to the specific apprentice rate [1][4][5].

rows.q: I was off sick from work in the UK on 2022-09-01. What was the weekly rate of statutory sick pay?
rows.answer: On 1 September 2022 in the UK, the weekly rate of Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) was £99.35 per week (for up to 28 weeks). [1][2]

rows.q: I was made redundant in the UK on 2019-05-01. What was the maximum amount of a week's pay used for statutory redundancy pay?
rows.answer: For redundancies on 2019-05-01, the statutory “week’s pay” cap (effective from 6 April 2019) was £525, so the maximum statutory redundancy pay was £15,750. [1][2]

rows.q: What was the weekly rate of statutory maternity pay in the UK on 2021-06-01?
rows.answer: On 2021-06-01, the weekly rate of statutory maternity pay in the UK was £151.97 [1][2][3]. This rate, which applied to the 33-week period following the initial six weeks of pay at 90 percent of average weekly earnings, came into effect on 4 April 2021 [1][2][3].

rows.q: My EU flight of 1,200 km was cancelled on 2019-03-01 without notice. How much compensation under EU261?
rows.answer: For a cancelled flight of 1,200 km, you are entitled to 250 EUR in compensation [1][2][3]. Under EU261, this amount applies to all flights of 1,500 km or less [1][4]. You may be eligible for this payment since you were given no notice of the cancellation [1][3]. The airline is only exempt from paying if they can prove the cancellation was caused by extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided [1][2]. If the airline offered you re-routing that arrived at your final destination less than two hours after the original scheduled time, this compensation could be reduced by 50% [1][3]

rows.q: My intra-EU flight of 2,000 km from Helsinki to Madrid was cancelled on 2022-05-10 at short notice. How much compensation under EU261?
rows.answer: For an intra-EU flight of 2,000 km cancelled at short notice, you are entitled to €400 in compensation under EU261 [1][2][3]. This amount applies to intra-Community flights longer than 1,500 km [4][5]. The airline may reduce this compensation by 50% to €200 if they offer re-routing that allows you to reach your final destination no more than three hours after the original scheduled arrival time [4][5][6]. You are not entitled to this compensation if the airline proves the cancellation was caused by extraordinary circumstances [4][2][5].

rows.q: Lentoni Helsingistä Berliiniin (noin 1 100 km) peruttiin 2023-09-01 ilman ennakkoilmoitusta. Paljonko korvausta saan EU-asetuksen 261/2004 mukaan?
rows.answer: EU-asetuksen 261/2004 vakiokorvaus peruutuksen tai viivästymisen/epäämisen yhteydessä riippuu lennon pituudesta. Helsingistä Berliiniin (n. 1 100 km) se on 250 € lennosta, jossa matka on 1 500 km tai alle, jos korvausoikeuden ehdot täyttyvät (esim. viivästys yli 3 h tai peruutus alle 14 vrk ennen lähtöä). [1][2]

rows.q: I sent a GDPR data access request on 2024-02-01. How long does the company have to respond?
rows.answer: A company must respond to a GDPR data access (subject access) request within one month of receiving it. This can be extended by up to two additional months if the request is complex, but they must notify you and give reasons for the delay before the initial one-month deadline expires. [1][2]

rows.q: My flight from Paris to New York (about 5,800 km) with an EU airline was cancelled without notice on 2021-11-03. How much EU261 compensation?
rows.answer: Your Paris–New York route is 5,800 km, so under EU261 Article 7 you fall in the “all flights not falling under €250/€400 tiers” category, which is €600 compensation for a cancellation. This applies unless the airline proves either you were informed at least two weeks before departure, or (if informed 2–7 days before) the re-routing timing meets the specific limits, or (if <7 days) it meets the tighter limits; also no compensation is due for “extraordinary circumstances” beyond the airline’s control. [1][2]

rows.q: My flight from Helsinki to Las Palmas de Gran Canaria (about 4,900 km, within the EU) was cancelled on 2024-01-15. How much EU261 compensation?
rows.answer:
For a flight from Helsinki to Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, which is an intra-EU flight of more than 1,500 km, the standard EU261 compensation is 400 EUR [1][2][3].

This amount applies because EU261 classifies all intra-Community flights longer than 1,500 km at the 400 EUR rate, regardless of the total distance exceeding 3,500 km [3][4]. You are entitled to this provided you were notified of the cancellation less than 14 days before departure and the cancellation was not caused by extraordinary circumstances [5][4]. The airline may reduce this compensation by 50% if they offered re-routing that

rows.q: Mein Flug von München nach Lissabon (ca. 1.900 km) wurde am 2022-07-14 kurzfristig annulliert. Wie viel Entschädigung steht mir nach der EU-Verordnung 261/2004 zu?
rows.answer:
Da Ihr Flug von München nach Lissabon eine Distanz von über 1.500 km aufweist und innerhalb der EU liegt, steht Ihnen bei einer kurzfristigen Annullierung gemäß EU-Verordnung 261/2004 ein Entschädigungsanspruch in Höhe von 400 Euro zu [1][2][3].

Dieser Anspruch gilt, sofern die Fluggesellschaft nicht nachweisen kann, dass die Annullierung auf außergewöhnliche Umstände zurückzuführen war [4][5]. Zudem entfällt der Anspruch, wenn Sie rechtzeitig vor dem Abflug informiert wurden oder Ihnen ein Ersatzflug angeboten wurde, der innerhalb der gesetzlich festgelegten Zeitrahmen am Zielort eintrifft [

rows.q: I am 17 and worked a part-time job in the UK on 2023-08-01. What was the minimum hourly wage for my age?
rows.answer: If you were 17 on 2023-08-01, your minimum hourly wage was £5.28 (National Minimum Wage for age 16–17), applicable from 1 April 2023 [1][2].

rows.q: I was 22 years old and working in the UK on 2023-06-01. Which hourly minimum wage applied to me?
rows.answer: On 2023-06-01, if you were 22 and working in the UK, you fell under the “National Minimum wage (21–22)” rate. That hourly minimum wage was £10.18 per hour (rate from 1 April 2023). [1][2]

rows.q: I was a first-year apprentice aged 19 in the UK on 2020-09-01. What was the apprenticeship minimum hourly rate?
rows.answer: On 1 September 2020 you would be paid the apprentice minimum hourly rate of £4.15 per hour (the UK apprentice rate applies to under-19 apprentices, and also to those aged 19+ in the first year; this rate was in force from 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2021). [1][2]

rows.q: What was the weekly rate of statutory paternity pay in the UK on 2020-06-01?
rows.answer: On 2020-06-01, the weekly rate of UK statutory paternity pay (SPP) was £151.20 per week (or 90% of average weekly earnings if lower) [1][2].

rows.q: Lähetin GDPR-tietopyynnön yritykselle 2023-05-02. Missä ajassa yrityksen on vastattava?
rows.answer: Yrityksen on vastattava GDPR-tietopyyntöön ilman aiheetonta viivytystä ja viimeistään kuukauden kuluessa pyynnön vastaanottamisesta. Määräaikaa voi pidentää enintään kahdella kuukaudella, jos pyyntö on monimutkainen, ja yrityksen on ilmoitettava lisäajan tarpeesta viimeistään kuukauden kuluessa pyynnön vastaanottamisesta [1][2][3]. Jos vastausta ei tule ajoissa, voit tehdä valituksen tietosuojaviranomaiselle [4].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2017-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer:
For an involuntary bumping from a US domestic flight that results in an arrival delay of more than two hours, you are entitled to denied boarding compensation equal to 400% of your one-way fare, up to a maximum of $2,150 [1][2][3]. 

This compensation applies provided you had a confirmed reservation, met all check-in requirements, and the bumping was not due to specific exceptions like aircraft downgrades or safety-related weight restrictions [1][2][3]. If the calculated 400% amount exceeds $2,150, the airline may cap the payment at that limit [1][3].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2018-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: For an involuntary bump on a domestic flight where the substitute transportation is scheduled to arrive more than two hours after your original arrival time, you are entitled to compensation equal to 400 percent of your one-way fare to your destination, capped at $2,150 [1][2][3]. Eligibility depends on whether the substitute flight was planned to arrive more than two hours late, rather than the actual arrival time [3]. You must have had a confirmed reservation and met all ticketing and check-in requirements to qualify for this payment [1][2][4].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2019-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: Because your domestic flight arrived more than two hours late, you are entitled to involuntary denied boarding compensation equal to 400% of your one-way fare, capped at a maximum of $2,150 [1][2][3]. This compensation applies if you were bumped involuntarily, had a confirmed reservation, checked in on time, and arrived at the gate on time, provided the bumping was not due to specific exceptions like aircraft substitution for safety or weight restrictions [1][2][3]. The amount is calculated based on the one-way price to your destination or first stopover [2][3][4].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2019-11-30; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: For a domestic flight where you were involuntarily bumped and arrived more than two hours late, you are entitled to compensation equal to 400% of your one-way fare to your destination, capped at $2,150 [1][2][3]. This assumes you were bumped due to an oversold flight, met all check-in and gate arrival requirements, and none of the specific policy exceptions—such as aircraft changes for safety or weight restrictions—applied [1][2][3]. The airline should have provided this payment via cash or check at the airport or within 24 hours of the incident [1][2].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2020-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: For a domestic US flight on 2020-06-01 where you were involuntarily bumped and arrived 3 hours late, you are entitled to denied boarding compensation of 400% of your one-way fare, capped at $1,350 [1]. While current caps have since increased to $2,150 [2][3], the regulations in effect on the date of your travel applied the $1,350 limit [4][1]. You are eligible for this payment provided you had a confirmed reservation, checked in on time, and were not bumped due to specific exceptions like aircraft substitution for safety or weight restrictions [2][5].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2021-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: For a domestic US flight where you were involuntarily bumped from an oversold flight and the substitute itinerary was planned to arrive about 3 hours later, you’re generally entitled to denied boarding compensation equal to 400% of your one-way fare, capped at $2,150 (assuming you meet the eligibility conditions and the substitute wasn’t within 2 hours). Compensation is based on the planned arrival delay of the substitute flight, not how long you waited. [1][2]

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2022-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: For a U.S. domestic oversold-flight involuntary bump, if the substitute flight arrives 3 hours late, that’s an “over 2 hours” arrival delay, so the denied boarding compensation is at least 400% of your one-way fare, capped at $2,150 [1][2]. (You only get no compensation if the alternate is scheduled to arrive within 1 hour of the original arrival time [1][2].)

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2023-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: Because your domestic flight arrived more than two hours late, you are entitled to involuntary denied boarding compensation equal to 400 percent of your one-way fare, capped at a maximum of $2,150 [1][2][3]. This assumes you were involuntarily bumped, had a confirmed reservation, and met all check-in and gate deadlines [1][4]. Airlines are required to pay this amount by check or cash, typically at the airport on the day of the incident or within 24 hours if you were already rebooked on a substitute flight [1][2].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2024-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: For a domestic flight where you are bumped involuntarily and the substitute transportation arrives more than two hours after your original scheduled arrival time, you are entitled to compensation equal to 400% of your one-way fare, capped at a maximum of $2,150 [1][2][3]. Since your flight arrived 3 hours late, you fall into this category [1][3][4]. This compensation is based on the one-way price of your ticket to your destination or first stopover [2][5][4]. If your ticket has no fare, it is based on the lowest cash fare charged for that class of service [4].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2025-01-21; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer:
Because your domestic flight arrived 3 hours late, you fall into the category for delays exceeding 2 hours [1][2][3]. You are entitled to denied boarding compensation equal to 400 percent of your one-way fare to your final destination, capped at $2,150 [1][2][4].

If your one-way fare was $500, you would be owed $2,000. If your one-way fare was $600, your entitlement would be $2,400, but the airline can limit this payment to the $2,150 cap [1][3]. You are eligible for this payment provided you met all check-in and boarding requirements [1][2].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2025-01-22; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: Because your substitute flight arrived three hours after your original scheduled arrival time, you are entitled to involuntary denied boarding compensation equal to 400 percent of your one-way fare, capped at a maximum of 2,150 dollars [1][2][3]. This compensation applies for domestic delays exceeding two hours [1][3]. You must have had a confirmed reservation, checked in on time, and arrived at the gate on time to qualify [1][4]. The airline is required to provide this payment to you by cash or check [5][2].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2025-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: If your original flight was domestic (departing from a U.S. airport) and the oversold bump made the substitute arrive 3 hours late (i.e., over 2 hours after the planned arrival time), the denied-boarding compensation is 400% of your one-way fare to your destination/first stopover, capped at $2,150 [1][2]. You’re not eligible if the bump was due to a smaller aircraft substitution (operational/safety), weight/balance limits, etc. [1].

rows.q: I was bumped from an oversold US domestic flight on 2026-06-01; the substitute flight arrived 3 hours late. How much compensation?
rows.answer: Because your domestic flight arrived more than two hours late, you are entitled to involuntary denied boarding compensation equal to 400% of your one-way fare, capped at a maximum of $2,150 [1][2][3]. To qualify, you must have had a confirmed reservation, checked in on time, and arrived at the departure gate on time [1][4]. This compensation is required provided your bumping was not due to specific exceptions like an aircraft change or weight and balance restrictions on small planes [1][5][2]. Payment should have been provided at the airport or within 24 hours [1][5].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2016-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On June 1, 2016, the National Living Wage for workers aged 25 and over was £7.20 per hour [1][2][3]. This rate came into force on April 1, 2016 [1][4][5].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2017-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On 2017-06-01, the National Living Wage for workers aged 25 and over in the UK was 7.50 pounds per hour [1][2][3].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2018-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On 1 June 2018, the National Living Wage (for workers aged 25 and over) in the UK was £7.83 per hour (it increased to this rate from 1 April 2018). [1]

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2019-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On 1 June 2019 in the UK, the National Living Wage for workers aged 25+ was £8.21 per hour [1][2].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2020-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: As you were 30 in the UK on 2020-06-01, you would be on the National Living Wage (for ages 25 and over), which was £8.72 per hour from 1 April 2020 [1].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2021-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: For UK work on 2021-06-01, the National Living Wage (for workers aged 23 and over) was £8.91 per hour [1][2].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2022-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On June 1, 2022, the National Living Wage for workers aged 23 and over was £9.50 per hour [1][2][3].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2023-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On 1 June 2023, the statutory National Living Wage for workers aged 23 and over in the UK was £10.42 per hour [1][2][3].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2024-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On 2024-06-01, the National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over was £11.44 per hour [1][2][3].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2025-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On 2025-06-01, the National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over was £12.21 per hour [1][2].

rows.q: I am 30 and worked in the UK on 2026-06-01. What was the national living wage per hour?
rows.answer: On 1 June 2026, the National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over was £12.71 per hour [1][2][3].

rows.q: My EU flight of 1,200 km was cancelled on 2006-06-01 without notice. How much EU261 compensation?
rows.answer: For a flight of 1,200 km cancelled without notice, you are entitled to EUR 250 in compensation under EU261 regulations, provided the cancellation was not caused by extraordinary circumstances [1][2][3]. This amount applies to all flights of 1,500 kilometres or less [1][2]. If the airline offered you re-routing that allowed you to reach your final destination less than two hours after the original scheduled arrival time, this compensation may be reduced by 50% to EUR 125 [1][3].

rows.q: My EU flight of 1,200 km was cancelled on 2012-06-01 without notice. How much EU261 compensation?
rows.answer: For an EU flight of 1,200 km cancelled on 2012-06-01 without notice (i.e., less than 14 days before departure), EU261 compensation is €250, unless the airline can prove the cancellation was due to extraordinary circumstances that could not be avoided. [1][2]

rows.q: My EU flight of 1,200 km was cancelled on 2018-06-01 without notice. How much EU261 compensation?
rows.answer: For an EU261 flight of 1,200 km cancelled on 2018-06-01 without notice (i.e., informed less than 14 days before departure), the compensation is EUR 250 per passenger, unless the airline can prove extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided [1][2].

rows.q: My EU flight of 1,200 km was cancelled on 2024-06-01 without notice. How much EU261 compensation?
rows.answer: For an EU261 flight cancellation, compensation is €400 for intra-EU flights of more than 1,500 km; flights 1,500 km or less are €250 and flights over 3,500 km are €600 [1][2][3]. Since your flight was 1,200 km (≤ 1,500 km), the EU261 compensation is €250, assuming you weren’t informed at least 2 weeks before departure and no extraordinary circumstances exemption applies [1].
